classification.difficultyReason: Check adjacency in varied figures, distinguishing overlapping sectors and different vertices.

content.prompt: Decide whether the marked angles in each diagram are adjacent.

spec.description: TS points upper-left, TV lower-left and TU right and slightly down. Single arc VTS; double arc STU.
spec.mathematics: The two marked sectors share TS without overlap.
spec.answerVisibility: Sector marks remain visible; classification is answer-only.

answer.worked: $\angle VTS$ and $\angle STU$ share vertex $T$ and arm $TS$, and do not overlap.

spec.description: GF vertical up, GI horizontal right and GH obliquely between them. Double arc FGH; single arc HGI.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent sectors share GH. No right-angle square is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Sector marks are givens; classification is answer-only.

answer.worked: $\angle FGH$ and $\angle HGI$ share vertex $G$ and arm $GH$, and do not overlap.

spec.description: Z-like chain M–N–O–P; single arc at N, double arc at O.
spec.mathematics: Marked angles MNO and NOP have distinct vertices. No parallelism is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: All grey source arcs are givens; completed classification is omitted.

answer.worked: $\angle MNO$ and $\angle NOP$ have different vertices, $N$ and $O$.

spec.description: N on the right joins M upper-left, L directly left and O lower-left. Double arc MNL; single arc LNO.
spec.mathematics: The marked angles share NL and have non-overlapping interiors.

answer.worked: $\angle MNL$ and $\angle LNO$ share vertex $N$ and arm $NL$, and do not overlap.

spec.description: QR left and slightly up, QS upper-left and QP nearly vertical up. Double outer arc spans RQP across QS; smaller single arc spans SQP.
spec.mathematics: SQP lies inside RQP. Preserve overlap rather than splitting the outer mark at QS.
spec.answerVisibility: Overlapping arcs remain student givens; classification is answer-only.

answer.worked: $\angle RQP$ and $\angle SQP$ overlap: $\angle SQP$ lies inside $\angle RQP$.

spec.description: KN and JL intersect at M. K upper-left, N lower-right, J lower-left and L upper-right. Double left arc JMK and single upper arc KML.
spec.mathematics: K–M–N and J–M–L are straight paths. Marked adjacent sectors share MK.
spec.answerVisibility: Marked sectors visible; completed response omitted.

answer.worked: $\angle JMK$ and $\angle KML$ share vertex $M$ and arm $MK$, and do not overlap.

spec.description: GF extends left and slightly up; GI right and slightly up; GH horizontally right. Broad single upper arc FGI; double narrow arc IGH.
spec.mathematics: GF and GH are not a straight path. Marked sectors share GI without overlap.

answer.worked: $\angle FGI$ and $\angle IGH$ share vertex $G$ and arm $GI$, and do not overlap.

spec.description: D–E–B lie on a rising diagonal; DC extends almost horizontally right. EA rises steeply from E. Double arc BDC at D; single arc AEB at E.
spec.mathematics: D and E remain distinct vertices. No numerical relationships are added.
spec.answerVisibility: Source angle marks visible; classification omitted.

answer.worked: $\angle AEB$ and $\angle BDC$ have different vertices, $E$ and $D$.

spec.description: DC upper-left, DF lower-left and DE vertically down. Double arc marks the smaller left sector CDF. Single outer arc runs from DC clockwise over the top and right to DE.
spec.mathematics: The outer mark explicitly represents reflex CDE, excluding the left sector containing DF. Reflex CDE and smaller CDF share DC without overlapping.
spec.answerVisibility: Reflex sweep and double left arc are student givens; classification is answer-only.

answer.worked: Reflex $\angle CDE$ and the smaller $\angle CDF$ share vertex $D$ and arm $DC$. The reflex sector passes around the top and right of $D$, so the marked interiors do not overlap.
